Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Keep the supplied language.", "input": "the seed exchange at the north library opened at nine on saturday and i brought six packets of calendula seeds from my garden the packets were labeled with the flower color and the month i collected them people could take seeds without leaving anything in return or trade packets if they preferred i helped arrange the tables near the front windows because the usual room was being painted one table held herbs and another had beans peas and squash a neighbor named marisol asked whether the calendula would grow in a balcony planter and i said they had done well in a pot that was about twelve inches wide we kept the seed list on a clipboard so visitors could write down what they took before lunch a volunteer counted the remaining envelopes and noticed that the printed supply receipt had been filed with the donation forms the actual cost was $59.21 not $111.48 the larger amount was from a different order for shelving and was not part of the seed exchange budget after we sorted the forms i took two packets of basil seeds for my windowsill and left the extra flower packets for the afternoon group the library staff said the room would be available again next month and the group planned to bring labels and small envelopes", "output": "The seed exchange at the North Library opened at nine on Saturday, and I brought six packets of calendula seeds from my garden. The packets were labeled with the flower color and the month I collected them. People could take seeds without leaving anything in return or trade packets if they preferred. I helped arrange the tables near the front windows because the usual room was being painted. One table held herbs, and another had beans, peas, and squash. A neighbor named Marisol asked whether the calendula would grow in a balcony planter, and I said they had done well in a pot that was about twelve inches wide. We kept the seed list on a clipboard so visitors could write down what they took. Before lunch, a volunteer counted the remaining envelopes and noticed that the printed supply receipt had been filed with the donation forms. The actual cost was $59.21, not $111.48. The larger amount was from a different order for shelving and was not part of the seed exchange budget. After we sorted the forms, I took two packets of basil seeds for my windowsill and left the extra flower packets for the afternoon group. The library staff said the room would be available again next month, and the group planned to bring labels and small envelopes."}]
